title: Machine-learning search surfaces extreme T-subdwarf candidate CWISE J0523
summary: A machine-learning-assisted search of WISE time-series images helped identify the high-proper-motion object CWISE J052306.42-015355.4. Its colors suggest an extreme T-subdwarf candidate, while spectral classification, parallax, distance and metallicity remain uncertain. Human and citizen-science pathways also contributed. The candidate result was public in the November 2021 preprint before the January 2022 journal article.
organization: Northern Arizona University; Caltech IPAC; Backyard Worlds: Planet 9; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

evidence.tested: Archival astrometry and multi-survey photometry support the object and candidate classification.
evidence.unknown: Spectroscopic classification and measured parallax are not established in the reviewed study.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning proper-motion search supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary v1 preprint metadata and abstract; NASA publication record, abstract, affiliations and journal date.
